brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from Qijingtang in western Luoyuan county, Fujian, with a national geographical indication; leaf from Qijingtang is blended with some from neighbouring villages.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is said to have been a tribute in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming and long sold well in Beijing and Tianjin. By tradition the name comes from a temple funded jointly by seven villages, each called a jing. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Tight, curved strands of a glossy, slightly grey green with visible specks.
taste_profile: Lasting fresh aroma of chestnut with a floral edge, and a full, fresh taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
